title: US Yield Repricing and Aggressive RBI VRRR Drains Frame Market Dynamics
changed: US economic signals diverged this week as slower Q2 GDP growth of 1.5% initially reinforced rate cut expectations and capped Treasury yields. Resilient July consumer spending and subsequent hawkish Fed rhetoric reversed that trajectory by week-end, pushing US yields higher and raising the risk of foreign institutional investment pressure on Indian equities. In corporate tech, Nvidia's $96bn quarter verified ongoing global AI infrastructure spending, balancing escalating compliance costs marked by Meta's $18bn legal settlement.

Domestically, the Reserve Bank of India shifted into aggressive liquidity absorption to keep short-term money market rates from falling below the policy corridor. The RBI followed a ₹1.42 lakh crore Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction at a 5.24% cutoff with a ₹6-lakh-crore VRRR drain. Despite this liquidity tightening, long-duration paper found firm support: institutional demand anchored the benchmark 10-year G-sec yield below 6.92%, backed by a 2.4x bid coverage ratio at the government's ₹34,000 crore bond auction.

Macroeconomic data pointed to an uneven domestic recovery. July IIP growth moderated to 6.7%, driven by infrastructure and corporate capex while mass consumer and rural demand trailed. Fiscal planning for the coming year took shape as the Finance Ministry set an October 12 pre-Budget timeline focused on revenue targets and fiscal restraint. For energy importers, a US pact controlling 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan crude altered medium-term global supply expectations, dampening upside risks for Brent crude.

threads.name: Fed Policy Repricing & US Yields
threads.note: Slower US Q2 GDP of 1.5% supported rate cut bets before hawkish Fed rhetoric pushed Treasury yields higher. Confirmed by sustained high US yields and FII equity outflows; broken by softer inflation readings that revive rate-cut consensus.

threads.name: RBI Short-Term Liquidity Absorption
threads.note: The RBI escalated VRRR drains from ₹1.42 lakh crore to ₹6 lakh crore to maintain the money market rate corridor. Confirmed by money market rates staying aligned with policy targets; broken by systemic liquidity deficits.

threads.name: India 10Y Sovereign Bond Anchoring
threads.note: Strong 2.4x bid coverage at the ₹34,000 crore auction held benchmark G-sec yields below 6.92%. Confirmed by institutional absorption of upcoming state debt; broken by spillovers from rising US Treasury yields.

threads.name: Global AI Infrastructure Capex
threads.note: Nvidia's $96bn quarter confirmed ongoing enterprise hardware investment. Confirmed by sustained mega-cap technology capex; broken by corporate spending pullbacks or regulatory hurdles.
